column1: # Search glossary: Estonian to English (ADR 0048). Written for Otos from Vision's scene-label
# names, the vocabulary search already reads photos with, then common words of a photo
# search (below). A line is an English reading, then the Estonian forms that mean it:
# nominative, then genitive (the stem compounds and case endings build on). A form is listed
# once, on the line of the sense it reads as: where it has several, the one a photo search
# means most often ("kell" is a clock before a bell, "aed" a garden before a fence), and the
# glossary does not load with a form listed twice. A form of three letters or fewer is read
# only as a whole word, so "kuus" (six) is not the moon ("kuu") with an ending.
# Common words of a photo search beyond the labels: people, colours, qualities, places, times
# and actions. A verb lists its stems as typed: the -v participle, the third person, -mas and
